# Setup

```{r setup}
# packages
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(nnet)

# read in data
wine <- read_csv('data/winequality-red.csv')
```

The data contain 11 chemical measurements for each of `r nrow(wine)` red wines, along with a quality score assigned by expert tasters. Very few wines get extreme scores:

```{r}
wine %>% count(quality)
```

So we'll group the scores into three classes: **low** (5 or below), **medium** (6), and **high** (7 or above). The column names also contain spaces, which are awkward in model formulas, so we'll replace them with underscores.

```{r}
# clean column names and define quality classes
wine <- wine %>%
  rename_with(~ str_replace_all(.x, ' ', '_')) %>%
  mutate(quality_group = cut(quality,
                             breaks = c(-Inf, 5, 6, Inf),
                             labels = c('low', 'medium', 'high'))) %>%
  select(-quality)

wine %>% count(quality_group)
```

Notice that the high class is much smaller than the other two. We'll come back to this later.

# Data partitioning

::: action
**Data partitioning**

1.  Copy the code chunk below into your script but do not run the resulting lines.
2.  Coordinate with your neighbor: choose a new RNG seed and input the same value in each of your scripts.
3.  Execute lines to partition the data.
:::

```{r}
# partition
set.seed(112425)
partitions <- wine %>%
  initial_split(prop = 0.8, strata = quality_group)

train <- training(partitions)
test <- testing(partitions)
```

The `strata` argument makes the split *stratified*: rows are sampled separately within each class, so the training and test sets keep the same class proportions. Without it, a random split could leave the test set with very few high-quality wines.

The predictors are measured on very different scales (density is always close to 1, while total sulfur dioxide ranges into the hundreds). We'll standardize them so that the coefficients are comparable. The means and standard deviations are computed from the training set **only** and then applied to both partitions.

```{r}
# standardize predictors using training-set means and SDs
rec <- recipe(quality_group ~ ., data = train) %>%
  step_normalize(all_predictors()) %>%
  prep()

train_std <- bake(rec, new_data = train)
test_std <- bake(rec, new_data = test)
```
